incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT — node=gpu-node-17 ephemeral-storage pressure detected (kubelet eviction threshold)

incident-bot: linked alert: /alerts/2056789012 — Pod model-cache-serve-7f9b eviction count spike

Mira Gomez: seeing a cascade of pod evictions on gpu-node-17 and gpu-node-18. model-cache containers OOM-ish logs then preemptive evict. paging in.

Raj Patel: @Mira can you paste the kubectl pod list for the node? thinking this is log bloat + cache fill.

Mira Gomez: yup — pulling now.
Mira Gomez: ```
kubectl get pods -o wide -n redwood-serving --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-node-17
NAME                         READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE   IP           NODE         NOMINATED NODE
model-cache-serve-7f9b       0/2     Evicted   3          2d   10.2.3.45    gpu-node-17   
logger-forwarder-6d8c       1/1     Running   0          5d   10.2.3.48    gpu-node-17   
api-proxy-rc-5f6g           1/1     Running   0          1d   10.2.3.49    gpu-node-17   
```

Mira Gomez: model-cache shows repeated exit code 137 then eviction. logs look noisy (rotating not keeping up).

Alice Chen: hitting similar on node-18. modelcache has big mmap files filling /var/lib/modelcache. Looks like aggressive prefetch + a runaway logging loop from cache-loader.

Raj Patel: error snippets?

Mira Gomez: here's tail from model-cache: ````
2026-03-15T09:42:11Z ERROR cache_loader.cpp:204 Prefetch failed: write failed, errno=28 (No space left on device)
2026-03-15T09:42:11Z WARN  kv_cache.cpp:118 drop leading entries, disk pressure
2026-03-15T09:42:12Z FATAL serve_runtime.cpp:87 cudaErrorIllegalAddress: an illegal memory access was encountered
````

Tom Burns: illegal address from CUDA may be secondary — when mmap/write fails the runtime can corrupt pointers during recovery. We should treat as customer-impacting until nodes stabilize.

CS Maya: any customer visible impact? Any ongoing requests failing?

Raj Patel: metrics: 12% of hosted generation requests routed to those nodes saw 500/502/504 spikes. p99 latency for text-gen increased from 110ms -> 780ms for the last 20m. Error rate up ~4.7% for model-x-prod.

Mira Gomez: current mitigation plan I'm starting: 1) cordon gpu-node-17/18 2) drain non-critical pods 3) restart model-cache daemonset with reduced prefetch config 4) truncate largest log files and rotate 5) rollaffected customers to fallback region/model variant.

Mira Gomez: executing step 1 now. `kubectl cordon gpu-node-17`

incident-bot: action logged by Mira Gomez at 09:45:20 — node cordoned.

Raj Patel: draining but leave api-proxy live. Use `--ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` carefully.

Mira Gomez: running drain: ```
kubectl drain gpu-node-17 -n redwood-serving --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

Mira Gomez: drained. starting forced restart of model-cache pods in the node's rs by scaling down to 0 then up.

Alice Chen: while that runs, deleting oldest rotated logs that are >10GB on node via ssh. I'm also applying a temp emptyDir size limit to model-cache to prevent it from doubling writes.

Tom Burns: put a temporary admission annotation to stop the prefetcher jobs from creating large mmap files: `service/model-cache: prefetch=off-temp` — deploy patch queued.

Mira Gomez: patch applied. model-cache replicas are coming back up with new config. initial pods are healthy-ish but still warning about low space.

Mira Gomez: truncating journal logs and stale core dumps: `sudo journalctl --vacuum-size=200M` and removing /var/crash/* older than 24h.

Raj Patel: good. keeping an eye on error rates. if still degrading, we'll route traffic away from region via Smart Router fallback.

CS Maya: notifying impacted customers with a short note: "We are investigating elevated errors and latency for some hosted inference; mitigation in progress. We'll update in 30m." Shall I send?

Mira Gomez: yes, please send. include the workaround: temporary fallback to smaller model variant (model-x-small) is available via parameter model_variant.

incident-bot: pager escalated to Raj Patel (oncall) at 09:55:02 — acknowledged.

Raj Patel: I'm taking the active handoff. Mira — you're running out in 20m?

Mira Gomez: I have a dentist at 10:20. I'll stay until 10:10 and then handoff to you. state: nodes cordoned, model-cache updated, logs rotated, pods restarted. error rate trending down from 4.7% -> 1.3% in last 8m.

Raj Patel: I'll continue. next steps: 1) uncordon once nodes cleaned and ephemeral pressure gone 2) schedule node reprovision to increase /var/lib capacity or convert to ephemeral PVC with eviction guard 3) add immediate alert for mmap growth > 6GB in 5m window.

Tom Burns: created infra ticket INF-4298 to increase emptyDir quota and add kubelet eviction tuning. also adding a cron to clean old models from /var/lib/modelcache every 6h.

Mira Gomez: handing off live: `handoff: Mira -> Raj at 10:09` — logs, commands, and patched config saved in incident runbook snippet.

Raj Patel: ack. I'll keep this open. current customer impact: reduced to ~0.9% error rate and most affected customers failing requests are being retried by the client. marking incident as mitigation-in-progress.

CS Maya: update sent to customers at 10:12 — they appreciate the quick notice.

incident-bot: incident note created: /incidents/2056789012 — Mitigated: temporary prefetch off, logs cleared, nodes cordoned & drained, follow-up infra ticket INF-4298.

Alice Chen: follow-up: add unit to the modelcache to self-throttle when disk writes hit >85% usage. filing follow-up task.

Raj Patel: thanks team. I'll keep monitoring for 1h then move to postmortem if stable. :thumbsup:

Mira Gomez: back on my calendar, leaving handoff docs in #eng-oncall.

incident-bot: thread closed by Raj Patel at 10:42:00 — monitoring continues.
